title: Use the slope formula
text: Since $$x=r cos\left(\theta\right)$$ and $$y=r sin\left(\theta\right)$$, the slope is $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{r'\sin\theta+r\cos\theta}{r'\cos\theta-r\sin\theta}$$

title: Plug in
text: At $$\theta=\frac{5\pi}{6}$$, $$r=4$$ and $$r'=8cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)=-4\sqrt{3}$$. Then $$r' sin\left(\theta\right)+r cos\left(\theta\right)=-2\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{3}=-4\sqrt{3}$$ and $$r' cos\left(\theta\right)-r sin\left(\theta\right)=6-2=4$$, so the slope is $$-\sqrt{3}$$.
